big_picture: Anthropic completed a record-breaking IPO raising over $80 billion at valuations reaching up to $2 trillion. Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115 billion to $116 billion, but faced a 35% stock drawdown amid executive scandals and US export controls to China. Federal Reserve meeting minutes revealed growing consensus among central bank officials for an interest rate hike at the December 9th meeting.

themes.title: Anthropic debuts in a record-breaking public offering
themes.explanation: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, raising over $80 billion and achieving market valuations between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. The company reported $2.6 billion in fiscal year 2025 revenue while having burned only $9 billion in total capital since inception. However, the listing compressed broader market valuations, and the firm faces $71 billion in spending commitments due over the coming year.

themes.title: Nvidia beats earnings expectations despite executive scandal and export bans
themes.explanation: Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115 billion to $116 billion, more than doubling its results from the previous year, and raised its 2028 growth guidance to 75%. Despite this outperformance, the stock dropped 35% from its highs following governance concerns surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang and new Commerce Department rules restricting Chinese firms from accessing remote chip servers. In response to trade pressures, Nvidia announced it will stop selling Hopper chips into China.

themes.title: Federal Reserve officials signal December interest rate increase
themes.explanation: Federal Reserve minutes and market indicators show an 85% probability of an interest rate hike at the upcoming December meeting, with officials weighing a 25 to 50 basis point increase. Central bankers are responding to persistent inflation, as 76% of Consumer Price Index components are rising faster than 2% annualized. Analysts warn that rate hikes combined with a $2 trillion annual federal deficit could reduce market liquidity.

themes.title: US manufacturing faces cost hurdles while trucking industry declines
themes.explanation: US manufacturing jobs remain difficult to restore because domestic labor costs are five times higher than in China, causing tariffs to shift factory production to countries like Vietnam instead. Industry experts recommend focusing US policy on high-tech sectors like semiconductors and biotech rather than low-cost assembly. Concurrently, the trucking industry is experiencing its worst downturn in 50 years due to shifting final-mile delivery models and municipal spending cuts.

concept_of_the_day.explanation: Key-person risk is the operational and financial vulnerability a company faces when its success and market valuation depend heavily on a single executive. If that leader steps down, faces legal scrutiny, or becomes involved in a public scandal, investor confidence can fall rapidly regardless of the company's current earnings. In today's sources, Nvidia suffered a 35% drawdown from its record highs following reports of executive scandal and board governance friction regarding former CEO Jensen Huang. Even though Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115 billion and maintained a 70% gross margin, key-person risk created market uncertainty about the firm's long-term leadership stability.

watch_for: Federal Reserve policy meeting and rate decision on December 9th
